paragraphs: Pulsara sells a secure app that unites the entire care team across different departments or organizations. The company describes the app as replacing multiple phone calls, radio reports, faxes, and pagers with one unified patient channel. Users named on the site run from EMS and hospital staff to urgent cares, nursing homes, testing clinics, standalone EDs, Public Health, and FEMA Medical Operations Coordination Cells.

For EMS teams, the site lists integration with ECG monitors, EMS-to-EMS handoff, facility-to-EMS handoff, and the ability to consult specialists or medical control. The about page describes the process as creating a dedicated patient channel, building the team, and communicating using audio, live video, instant messaging, data, images, and key benchmarks. Clinicians can add a new organization, team, or specialist to any patient event as the patient condition and location change. The site states that Pulsara is SOC2 Type 2 and ISO 27001 certified and an approved vendor with many national health systems.

quote.text: Pulsara is the communications and logistics platform that unites distributed teams and fragmented technologies as dynamic events evolve.
